key_insight: The paper couples phase-field fracture with discrete differential geometry so crack growth and large shape change can be simulated consistently on highly deformable thin structures.
engineering_relevance: This enables damage-tolerant design and failure prediction for flexible sheets, membranes, and flexible-electronics geometries where deformation and fracture strongly interact.
method: Phase field is defined on a triangulated midsurface and coupled to discrete membrane and bending energies.
A staggered solver with an active-set constraint enforces crack irreversibility.
A degradation-deletion step removes nearly failed elements and updates the DDG topology to allow full crack opening and post-fracture reconfiguration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with geometrically nonlinear finite elements for 2D fracture and successful capture of 3D tearing phenomena, including crack convergence/coalescence and island-bridge snap-through behavior.
watch_item: The degradation-deletion and topology reconstruction steps may be sensitive to mesh quality and thresholds, so robustness and parameter calibration are important.
paper_title: Phase-Field Fracture Simulation of Highly Deformable Thin Structures via a Discrete Differential Geometry Framework
